title: policy.json: env
description: The environment resource manager: worktrees, dev-server ports, serial-resource locks and secrets (design part 13.2).

worktree_setup.description: Commands run, in order, in a fresh worktree by `hitld env setup`: install from the lockfile, copy .env.example files, generate code. Each runs through the shell, so this is owner configuration, never agent input. A failing command stops the setup and is reported before the executor starts. The merge queue runs merge.fast_checks and merge.full_suite in a fresh worktree of its own after these same commands, so they must make everything those checks need that git does not track: the install, and any generated, uncommitted files the checks import. With those checks set and this empty, `hitld check policy`, `hitld config explain` and `hitld install` warn, naming the install for the lockfile they find, and the queue stops before it checks a branch when its worktree has a lockfile but not the directory its install makes (node_modules, .venv), refusing no branch.
worktree_setup.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell in the new worktree

worktree_root.description: The directory that holds the worktrees, one subdirectory per holder. Absolute, or relative to the repository root. When absent, worktrees live in the private store under worktrees/, outside the repository. An absolute path moved to the machine file (design part 13.4) and still loads here, with a warning; a relative path names a subdirectory under the machine's root once the machine file sets one.

port_range.description: Dev-server ports are leased from this inclusive range. A port already in use on the machine is skipped, whoever uses it. Moved to the machine file (design part 13.4); here it still loads, with a warning, until the machine file sets it, and after that it can only narrow the machine's range.

failed_worktrees_kept.description: How many worktrees of failed dispatches are kept for inspection. The oldest beyond this are removed, after any uncommitted change is saved to the branch.

serial_resources.description: The resources that one holder at a time may use, machine-wide: locks are refused on any other name, so a typo cannot silently hold nothing.

lock_expiry_seconds.description: The limit, in seconds since its last renewal, for a lock whose holder's liveness cannot be checked (a holder on another host, or one whose process start time cannot be read): past it, such a lock counts as stale. A holder whose process is alive and can be told to be the very one it was taken for keeps its lock past this limit; a hung one is ended by `hitld env unlock --force` or the watchdog. A lock whose holder process has gone, whose process ID was reused or whose machine restarted is stale at once.

secret_provider.description: Where secret values are read from: the operating system's keychain (macOS Keychain, or the Secret Service on Linux), the HITLD_SECRET_<NAME> environment variables of the process running hitld (for CI), or auto (the keychain, then the environment). Moved to the machine file (design part 13.4); here it still loads, with a warning, until the machine file sets it, and after that it can only narrow auto to keychain or env.

secret_tasks.description: The only way a secret is used (design part 13.2). Each entry is a named task: a fixed command, the roles that may run it and the secrets it receives. `hitld env exec <task>` runs it with those secrets in its environment and nothing else; an agent can name a task but never choose the command, its arguments or the secrets. A task is code with access to secrets, so the owner reviews every entry here as carefully as a change to a script that deploys. Keep the command narrow (a fixed script, not a shell or an interpreter that takes the agent's input), and remember it runs with the secrets in the directory named by cwd: use `repo` (the primary checkout, which the owner controls), and `worktree` only when the command cannot be steered by the files there. With no tasks, no secret is available to anyone.

task.description: The task's name, which `hitld env exec` takes.

roles.description: The roles that may run it. The role is read from the dispatch record the orchestrator wrote, never from the caller.

secrets.description: The secret names the task receives, which are also the environment variable names its process sees.

argv.description: The exact command: the program (an absolute path, so the caller's PATH cannot redirect it) then its arguments. Run without a shell. Give this or repo_script.
argv.x-hitld-executes: the command is run with the task's secrets in its environment

repo_script.description: Instead of argv: a fixed script path inside the primary checkout (not the executor's worktree), run directly. It must be executable and stay inside the repository. Give this or argv.
repo_script.x-hitld-executes: the script is run with the task's secrets in its environment

cwd.description: Where it runs: the primary checkout (repo), or the dispatch's own worktree.

secret_tasks.x-hitld-executes: each task's argv or repo_script is run with the task's secrets in its environment
